S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers must report to the relevant regulator any thermal incident involving overheating, fire, or suspected thermal runaway within 5 calendar days of learning of it. An incident presenting an imminent risk of injury or spread of fire must be reported within 24 hours. Manufacturers must notify affected customers within 5 calendar days when an incident indicates a material safety risk for their unit or model; urgent risks require notice within 24 hours.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: Each model must undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C using a regulator-approved protocol, a representative sample, and documented failure criteria. Manufacturers must submit per-model results, including protocol, sample size, and failure rate, to the regulator at certification and after a material design change. Results must be provided to customers considering or owning the model, but individual-company per-model failure rates must not be published to the general public. A failure rate above 5% requires a regulator-reviewed corrective-action plan and follow-up testing; it does not by itself bar certification or sale.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: New units must support remote emergency shut-off at installation. Manufacturers must provide a safe, secure shut-off capability for installed units that lack it within 6 years of adoption, where technically feasible; if it is not feasible for a unit, the manufacturer must notify its owner and regulator and provide an equivalent safety measure or replacement plan.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: New units must include built-in fire suppression beginning 36 months after adoption. The requirement must be verified through testing under a regulator-approved protocol.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: A model exceeding 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in any year triggers prompt regulator verification, investigation, and a manufacturer corrective-action plan with a defined timetable. Following verification, the regulator must require a recall when the evidence indicates an unacceptable safety risk, or when the manufacturer fails to complete adequate corrective action on time. Customers must receive clear safety notices about hazards relevant to their model, recommended precautions, and any corrective action, promptly and within 24 hours for an urgent risk or 5 calendar days for other material safety risks.

document.section_notes: S1 is strict (24h serious, 5d other, 24h urgent customer notice). S2 has 55°C test, results to customers/regulators but not public, yet above 5% only requires corrective action, not a sales stop. S3 requires new-unit shut-off immediately and retrofit within 6 years with feasibility alternative. S4 requires built-in suppression at 36 months. S5 has an 8/100k corrective-action trigger with open-ended corrective alternative instead of mandatory recall, and 5-day notice.
